    Compounded semaglutide price: what online clinics charge.

    Peptide Chooser editorial team. Checked 8 Nov 2026.

    Short answer

    Compounded semaglutide from $49/mo at 28 clinics1, checked 8 Nov 2026. Plans run from $49 to $369 a month (37 plans)1, against $149 to $650 for Wegovy2. Compounded semaglutide is a pharmacy-made copy, not FDA approved, and the FDA does not check its safety, effectiveness or quality before it is sold.3 The FDA has warned about dosing errors and about versions made from salt forms of semaglutide.4

    What is compounded semaglutide?

    Semaglutide is the medicine in Wegovy.23 Compounded semaglutide is a copy made by a pharmacy for a patient with a prescription. It is not FDA approved: the FDA does not check a compounded medicine's safety, effectiveness or quality before it is sold.3

    While semaglutide was in short supply, pharmacies could make copies of it. Semaglutide is no longer on the FDA's drug shortage list, and for state-licensed pharmacies the time the FDA allowed for copies ended on 22 April 2025.24 Online clinics still sell compounded plans. Our guide on compounded vs brand GLP-1 explains the rules.

    What is the care fee?

    Many clinics charge for the medicine and for the care around it: the prescriber, the check-ins and messages. Some fold it into one price, some add it as a monthly membership.

    Of the 37 plans, 4 say the price is all-in and 2 add a monthly fee. At Zealthy, $151 for the medicine plus $135 for care makes $286 a month.5 For 31 plans the clinic's page did not show whether a fee is added, so ask before you sign up.

    What does a lower price not tell you?

    • The dose. Ask whether the price goes up when the dose goes up.
    • The care fee, if it is charged on top.
    • Which pharmacy makes it, and whether the clinic tells you.
    • Whether it is semaglutide or a salt form. The FDA says salt forms such as semaglutide sodium and semaglutide acetate are different ingredients from the one in the approved drugs.4
    • Whether the clinic has had an FDA warning letter. The table shows the newest one.

    What has the FDA warned about?

    The FDA has had reports of side effects, some needing a hospital stay, that may be linked to dosing errors with compounded semaglutide injections: patients measuring the wrong amount, and sometimes prescribers working out the dose wrong.4

    It has also had reports from people given compounded semaglutide in doses beyond the approved label. Most pharmacies do not have to report side effects to the FDA, so the FDA says these are likely under-reported.4

    None of this is medical advice. Your prescriber can tell you which medicine and which dose fit you.

    Questions about compounded semaglutide

    What is compounded semaglutide?

    A copy of semaglutide, the medicine in Wegovy, made by a pharmacy for a patient with a prescription. It is not FDA approved: the FDA does not check a compounded medicine's safety, effectiveness or quality before it is sold.

    How much does compounded semaglutide cost?

    Compounded semaglutide from $49/mo at 28 clinics, checked 8 Nov 2026. Plans run from $49 to $369 a month (37 plans), against $149 to $650 for Wegovy.

    Is compounded semaglutide FDA approved?

    No. Compounded semaglutide is a pharmacy-made copy, not FDA approved, and the FDA does not check its safety, effectiveness or quality before it is sold.

    Can pharmacies still make compounded semaglutide?

    Semaglutide is no longer on the FDA's drug shortage list, and for state-licensed pharmacies the time the FDA allowed for copies ended on 22 April 2025. Online clinics still sell compounded plans.

    What has the FDA warned about?

    Dosing errors with compounded semaglutide injections, some of them needing a hospital stay, and versions made from salt forms such as semaglutide sodium and semaglutide acetate, which the FDA says are different ingredients from the one in the approved drugs.
